scope: Corollary 4.8 (Small mass of bad directions) of the manuscript “The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions” (preprints/The-Falconer-distance-conjecture-in-all-dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 073 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 98a7e721547308b9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the parameters of Theorem 4.1. There are c1, ϵ1 > 0 such that the following holds at sufficiently small δ. Let µ be a bounded point probability satisfying the t-ball bound with loss δ−ϵ1 . Let Bδ be the set of directions for which at most δ−q−c1 width-Cδ tubes capture µ-mass at least δc1 . There is a Borel set B+ δ ⊃ Bδ, depending only on the point law and this geometric test, such that every direction subprobability ν satisfying the q-ball bound with loss δ−ϵ1 , and, when q = k − 1, Equation (4.1) with ϵ1 in place of ϵ, satisfies ν(B+ δ ) ≤ δc1 . In particular this bounds the outer ν-measure of the original geometric bad set. The direction law need not be normalized on either set or on any individual incidence fiber. All predetermined fixed widths are allowed.
